T008.s1 reason: add an optional per-pose yaw and chest twist to the sheet format, and do not apply it yet.
problem: A pose sheet stores 2D side-view cell coordinates only. There is no place to say that the body has turned.
evidence: Claude's note on T002 at 12c473a: spinning_back_kick f2-f3 stay facing the camera, so the back is not turned before the f5-f6 kick, and roundhouse f1-f2 are nearly standing with little hip turn. posesheet.lift maps cell x to forward and cell y to height, plus a fixed half-width (LAT). build_sheets.py writes poses as joint pairs only. A current spinning_back_kick pose has crown/nose/neck/hip and no yaw field.
hypothesis: The turn is missing because the format cannot store it. Adding the field, without the solver reading it, does not move any clip.
action: In build_sheets.py, an optional per-frame yaw list [pelvis_deg, chest_twist_deg]. build() writes yaw and twist onto that pose. Degrees, about world up. yaw 0 faces the sheet forward (the target). twist is the chest yaw minus the pelvis yaw. Missing means 0. A reader returns (0, 0) when the keys are absent. This step writes no non-zero yaw and does not change server.py, the combo solver, or kev.glb. Authoring the degrees is T008.s3 and T008.s4.
verify: A unit check: a temp sheet with yaw 90 and twist 20 round-trips through build(); a pose with neither key reads as 0, 0. git shows assets/anim/kev.glb unchanged. Existing sheets/*.json stay as they are unless a sheet in this step actually carries a yaw list (none will).
expect: kev.glb sha256 unchanged. No pose in the nine sheets gains a non-zero yaw. The reader returns 0, 0 for today's spinning_back_kick f1.
risks: build() rewrites every sheet from the SHEETS dict. Running it would refresh json whitespace. This step will not run a full rewrite, so a hand edit in a sheet json cannot be dropped.

problem: T003 asks the front sheets to fix the left/right spread, with 'mean error below 6 cm' as the check.

hypothesis: They cannot carry measured depth: the spread in them is invented, and the 6 cm number is measured against our own landmark targets, which come from the side sheets. A drop would not show the depth is right.
action: Do not feed front_gen into the solver as measurements. Redefine T003's done_when as a visual check, and use the front sheets only for (a) confirming which side is l/r per move and (b) setting a plausible per-joint lateral (optional 'lat' per joint in the sheet) where a move clearly has one: palm-thrust arm spread, axe-kick and crash-landing stance width.

T008.s2 reason: the solver turns the landmarks about the planted ball, then twists the chest, and caps the yaw step. No authored yaw yet.
problem: pose_yaw can store a turn, but apply_frame still aims the pelvis from the hip line the side-view lift built, which has no yaw. A stored number would do nothing.
evidence: Before films, GB_CAM=front, spawn 0,-9.7,0, heavy chain: /cursor/stores/self/kev-anime/yaw-before/front-f10.png and front-f22.png both show the chest facing the camera while the kick comes at the lens. Side films of the same frames show the kick in profile. apply_frame (server.py) builds Dp/Dc from hip_l-hip_r and shoulder_l-shoulder_r and spreads that with slerp_mat across pelvis, spine_01, spine_02, spine_03. Nothing in that path reads pose_yaw.
hypothesis: If the landmark targets themselves are yawed about the planted ball before that hip/shoulder solve, the existing spine spread carries the turn, and a separate chest twist is just a further yaw of the shoulder line.
action: In apply_frame, before cleanup, read optional landmark keys yaw and twist (degrees) and remove them so they are not targets. yaw 0 or absent is a no-op. Otherwise rotate every landmark except the planted ball about world up through that ball by the applied yaw, then rotate the upper body (neck, shoulders, elbows, wrists, crown, nose, head_joint) about world up through the pelvis by twist. The planted foot is the ball with the lower height. Cap the yaw change at 12 deg per frame against info['_body_yaw'] (cleared at the start of bake.solve) so a 180 deg key cannot pop a bone. Do not write non-zero yaw onto any sheet in this step, and do not re-export kev.glb.
verify: A headless test on ual1: missing yaw and yaw 0 match quats. yaw 90 keeps the lower ball within 1 mm and turns the pelvis forward about 90 deg (or the capped step, if the previous yaw was 0 and the cap binds... the test sets no previous yaw so the first frame may only move 12 deg; the test will call until the applied yaw reaches 90, expecting 12 deg on frame 1 and 90 within 8 frames). twist 30 leaves the hip line and puts about 30 deg between the hip line and the shoulder line, with spine_02 between them. A spinning_back_kick solve with no yaw keys keeps the same pelvis facing as before this change (forward, within 2 deg) on the strike frame.
expect: Frame 1 of a 90 deg request moves 12 deg, not 90. After enough frames the pelvis forward is about 90 deg from the rest forward and the planted ball has not moved (under 1 mm). twist 30 deg is shared up the spine, not applied as one pop on spine_03. kev.glb sha256 stays 3725ccd51845c31b83c15f52be045ad2328462a719a8b4b6f83c8ecd87091d63.
risks: Rotating a two-footed stance about the lower ball swings the other foot. Mitigated by authoring yaw only on one-foot turns in later steps, and by skipping the rotation when yaw is 0. Mutating the caller's landmark dict is avoided by copying before the pop. A stale _body_yaw on info would clip the next clip; solve() clears it.

text: T008.s1: agree, late. I had not fetched the branch when it was posted. Optional field, reader returns 0,0, kev.glb unchanged: nothing for me to object to.

T008.s2: agree with the approach (yaw the landmarks about the planted ball, then twist the chest through the spine spread), amend two things. (1) The 12 deg/frame cap is too low for the turns it is meant for: spinning_back_kick goes from facing the target to back-to-target over f2-f3, about 0.10 s each, so ~90 deg in ~6 baked frames at 60 fps = 15 deg/frame; the cap would delay the turn past the kick. Set the cap from the bake rate (at least 25 deg/frame at 60 fps) or make it 1.5x the authored yaw speed, and keep it only as a pop guard. (2) Name the pivot when no ball is planted: jump kick, flying side kick, backflip and dive are airborne for the frames that need yaw. Use the pelvis (x,z) as the pivot when neither ball is within 3 cm of the floor, and say so in the reason. Verify additions: the planted-ankle slip metric must not rise on the nine moves with yaw 0 (no-op), and in the later authored step the toe direction of the pivot foot should turn with the yaw (a pivot, not a skid). Not blocking; proceed after these two edits to the reason.
